rounds.text: Oswal Green Tech Ltd is trading at a heavily discounted valuation, highlighted by a remarkably low price-to-book ratio of 0.21x based on a share price of ₹ 19.6 against a book value of ₹ 92.9 [E2], which is further underscored by a sector benchmark comparison showing a P/B of 0.29x against 1.31x [E7]. This disconnect between market value and underlying assets occurs alongside an attractive trailing P/E ratio of 12.9 [E1]. Operational efficiency closely matches sector norms, with the company delivering a return on assets of 1.85% compared to the sector benchmark of 1.92% [E8]. Conceded: the company has delivered a poor sales growth of -20.1% over past five years [E60], a year-over-year sales decline of -77% [E69], negative compounded profit growth over 10, 5, and 3 years [E18, E19, E20], a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4], and a depressed stock price sitting only 4% of the way up its 52-week range [E5].

The bull case leans heavily on statistical cheapness, but the multi-year fundamentals tell a story of structural decay rather than a genuine value opportunity. Compounded profit growth has contracted over every medium- and long-term horizon, registering -5% over 10 years, -12% over 5 years, and -11% over 3 years [E18, E19, E20]. This persistent earnings erosion is compounded by a poor sales growth rate of -20.1% over the past five years and a staggering one-year sales contraction of -77% YoY [E60, E69]. Furthermore, the stock offers a zero dividend yield of 0.00%, meaning patient capital receives no cash return while waiting for a turnaround [E4]. The stock sits merely 4% above its 52-week low within a depressed range of 19 to 44, reflecting deep market skepticism that is fully justified by the deteriorating top line [E5]. Conceded: the trailing twelve months show a sharp 269% profit growth and low headline valuation multiples such as a 0.21x price-to-book ratio [E2, E21].

Conceded: compounded profit growth over 10, 5, and 3 years is negative [E18, E19, E20], along with a 5-year sales growth of -20.1% [E60], a 1-year sales contraction of -77% YoY [E69], a zero dividend yield [E4], and a stock price sitting just 4% above its 52-week low [E5]. However, the bear dismisses the inflection point too quickly; trailing twelve-month profit growth has exploded by 269% [E21], vastly outperforming the sector median profit growth of 25.0% [E75]. This massive earnings acceleration has triggered positive price-led signals showing profit growth exceeding 1-year price growth by 317% as expectations start to outperform [E55]. Such a fundamental turnaround renders historical multi-year contractions obsolete, especially when backed by screen reasons highlighting accelerating earnings and YoY profit growth above 20% [E66, E68]. Trading at a deeply discounted price-to-book ratio of 0.21x against a sector benchmark of 1.31x [E2, E7], the market is pricing in perpetual decay while ignoring a live, triple-digit earnings recovery [E21].

Conceded: trailing twelve-month profit growth has reached 269% [E21], outpacing the sector median of 25.0% [E75], and triggered positive price-led signals [E55] alongside screen reasons for accelerating earnings [E66, E68]. However, celebrating this single-period TTM inflection ignores a severe, multi-year structural decay defined by a 10-year compounded profit growth of -5% [E18], a 5-year rate of -12% [E19], and a 3-year rate of -11% [E20]. Furthermore, this temporary profit spike sits on top of catastrophic top-line deterioration, characterized by a 5-year poor sales growth of -20.1% [E60] and a staggering 1-year sales contraction of -77% YoY [E69]. The market prices this asset at a deep 0.21x price-to-book ratio [E2] precisely because the stock is pinned near the absolute bottom of its annual range at 4% of its 52-week spread [E5] and returns a flat 0.00% dividend yield [E4]. A volatile TTM earnings burst [E21] cannot erase a decade of profit contraction [E18] and a 77% collapse in annual sales [E69], leaving the low valuation fully justified by persistent fundamental risks.
